task_plan.metric_rationale: fbeta (beta=2.24, weighting recall): the description gives fp=1 / fn=5 (stated), a 5x asymmetry, so a symmetric metric would optimise the wrong error. Decision threshold 0.167. Rationale for the ratio: "5x" states an explicit magnitude and the text names a missed case as the costly error, giving fp=1 / fn=5. The decision threshold moves to 0.167 accordingly.

objective.rationale: "churn" asks for a discrete label/decision, so a threshold will be applied to the score.

cost_ratio.rationale: "5x" states an explicit magnitude and the text names a missed case as the costly error, giving fp=1 / fn=5. The decision threshold moves to 0.167 accordingly.

capacity_k.rationale: No acting capacity mentioned, so every prediction is assumed actionable and the metric scores the full test set. If your team can only work a fixed number of cases, say so - it changes the metric.

latency_budget_ms.rationale: "50ms" is a per-prediction serving budget of 50ms, which rules out models that cannot score a single row that fast.

interpretability_required.rationale: No explainability requirement mentioned, so model choice is assumed free to favour accuracy over transparency. Say so if a human has to justify each decision.

is_forecast.rationale: Nothing indicates a future time period, so rows are assumed exchangeable and a random split is valid. Say "forecast" or "time series" if the target is a future value.

protected_attributes.rationale: No protected or sensitive attribute named, so no fairness constraint is applied. Name the attributes explicitly (e.g. "don't discriminate by gender") to enable fairness auditing.

task_spec.raw_text: Predict which customers will churn so the retention team can intervene. Missing a churner costs about 5x a false alarm, and scoring must respond in under 50ms.
